text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions instead of short, confusing ones. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused, so each one does only one job. This makes code much easier to test and fix. Clean code also improves maintainability, which means other developers can update it later without breaking things. In short, writing clean code saves time and reduces mistakes for the whole team.
